title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-priya-2026-03-04
content:
Quick back-of-the-envelope notes on token math, unit economics, and simple tier ideas. Mostly drafting numbers to sanity-check pricing assumptions for hosted API and embeddings.

Context / goals:
- Keep a simple free / starter / pro / enterprise progression that maps to usage patterns we see in PLG funnel.
- Aim for healthy gross margins after infra + ops, but still competitive vs public LLM APIs.
- Provide clear overage and burst rules.

Assumptions (rough):
- Typical gen model (13B-ish quantized): infra cost ~ $2 per 1M tokens (includes GPU amortized, networking, storage, overhead). Range: $1.5 - $4.
- Larger model (70B): infra cost ~ $12 per 1M tokens. Range: $8 - $20.
- Embedding model: infra cost ~ $0.50 per 1k embeddings (per 1k vector ops). Range: $0.3 - $1.0 depending on dimension & batching.
- Support + infra SRE + platform overhead allocation target: add 10-15% of revenue to cover non-infra (monitoring, logging retention, console infra). For first-pass margin calc I'll treat as a fixed multiplier on price rather than per-token.

Token math examples:
- 1M tokens = 1,000,000 tokens. If average request is 900 tokens (750 prompt + 150 completion), that's ~1,111 requests per million tokens.
- If average prompt+resp ~ 300 tokens (search + short responses), that's ~3,333 requests per million tokens.

Per-unit cost (example table):
- Small/gen model cost: $2 / 1M tokens -> $0.000002 per token -> $0.002 per 1k tokens.
- Mid/gen model cost: $10 / 1M tokens -> $0.00001 per token -> $0.01 per 1k tokens.
- Large/gen model cost: $20 / 1M tokens -> $0.00002 per token -> $0.02 per 1k tokens.

Simple pricing sketches (hosted API, metered):
1) Free tier: 10k tokens/month free credit (one-time trial). Low friction for devs to integrate.
2) Starter: $19 / month -> 1M tokens included -> price per 1M = $19. Infra cost (small model) $2 -> gross contribution per 1M = $17 -> ~89% gross margin before ops. Overages: $0.025 per 1k tokens ($25 per 1M) if user exceeds included allocation (encourages moving to Pro if heavy usage).
3) Pro: $199 / month -> 15M tokens included -> price per 1M = $13.27. Infra cost $2 -> contribution per 1M = $11.27 -> ~85% gross margin. Overage: $0.02 per 1k tokens ($20 per 1M).
4) Business / Team tier: $999 / month -> 100M tokens included -> price per 1M = $9.99. Infra cost $2 -> contribution = $7.99 -> ~80% margin. Add team seats, advanced analytics, logs retention as add-ons.
5) Enterprise / Dedicated: custom pricing (volume discounts + reserved capacity). Example: committed 1B tokens/year -> effective $5 per 1M tokens with dedicated pool / SLA. If they want VPC/private, add platform fee and support retainer.

Embeddings pricing sketch:
- Cost: $0.50 per 1k embeddings (infra) -> Charging price $1.50 per 1k embeddings (list price) leaves ~$1.00 per 1k margin (~66%).
- Starter embedding pack: $49 / month -> 50k embeddings. Overage: $0.002 per embedding (i.e., $2 per 1k).

Unit economics worked example (Starter):
- Revenue: $19 / month from a user who uses exactly 1M tokens.
- Infra cost: $2.00. Platform ops allocation (~12% of revenue) = $2.28. Payment fees + misc = $0.50 (estimate). Total costs ~ $4.78. Gross profit ~ $14.22 -> ~75% contribution margin (after ops allocation).
- CAC payback: if CAC is ~$200 (PLG + self-serve + some content spend), payback on revenue alone is slow. Important to upsell to Pro/Team or convert to reserved capacity. So focus on expansion motions.

Sensitivity notes:
- If infra cost for heavier models rises to $12/1M, margins compress badly. That's where routing + fallbacks help (route to cheaper model variants for low-risk requests).
- Batching, prefix caching and KV reuse can materially reduce tokens served (effective tokens paid), increases margin.

Overage and throttling rules (draft):
- Soft overage: bill at tier overage rate up to 200% of included for Starter/Pro then throttle (prevent surprise bills).
- Burst credits: short bursts allowed if we have capacity, billed at higher per-token price.
- Rate limits: requests/sec limits per tier; allow burst windows.

Tier naming / features (quick):
- Free: 10k tokens, email support, community forum, 30-day usage history
- Starter ($19): 1M tokens, 30-day logs, basic console, rate limit 5 rps
- Pro ($199): 15M tokens, 90-day logs, advanced analytics, higher rate limits 50 rps, team invites
- Team ($999): 100M tokens, 1y logs, SSO, audit logs, higher SLA, priority support
- Enterprise: dedicated pools, private deploy, SLA, custom billing

Behavioral pricing levers to test:
- Charge for context window length (e.g., >8k context priced higher) or auto-route long context to cost-optimized models but expose tradeoffs.
- Add per-route configuration: lower-latency/expensive models opt-in with higher price.
- Volume discounts for committed spend (monthly/annual).

Open questions / to-do:
- Get more precise infra cost curves by model family and qps patterns (SRE + infra team input).
- Simulate churn and expansion to estimate LTV:CAC under these price points.
- Decide whether to simplify to per-1k pricing instead of token bundles (customers like predictability vs. simplicity).
- Validate embedding cost assumptions vs actual vectorization throughput numbers.

Notes to self: keep pricing language simple on the website: show $/1M token equivalent and example use cases (e.g., 1M tokens ~= 1,100 mid-length chats).

References / links: Confluence / Jira to follow-up for infra cost runs and price experiments (TODO list below).
